reaction: A clear, satisfying first construction step.

effect: The insert produced a refrigerated case; the remaining packs appear to be the next requirement.
reaction: The result is as expected, with no explanation yet of how the insert and packs work together.
reason: The freezer can prepare the packs, and this is the only gameplay action offered.
expectation: The packs will be chilled for use in or with the case.

effect: The packs are charged for temporary heat absorption; active refrigeration restores their capacity, clarifying their role during transfer.
reaction: That distinction is useful and makes the two cooling components make sense.
reason: Putting the conditioned packs into the case should complete the cold transport setup; it is the only gameplay action offered.
expectation: The result will be a prepared cold case for the core.

effect: The conditioned packs completed the buffered field case and the chapter goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to finish a tangible tool for preserving the fragile sample, though the final result has little detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Charging the cold packs explained how they buffer incoming heat temporarily and why active refrigeration is still needed; that made the case more than a list of parts.

leastWorthwhile.text: The shell and insulation actions were sensible but predictable, with little feedback beyond the created item names.

surprise.text: The distinction between the packs' limited heat absorption and refrigeration restoring that capacity clarified how the cooling system works.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; fitting the refrigeration insert initially left its relationship to the packs unclear, but the next result helped explain it.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see whether the case helps retrieve an intact sample and what the ridged fragment turns out to be. The assembly itself was rather linear.
